title: Functional Data Strengthen Clinical Validation of PhenoScore Phenotype-Guided AI for ANKRD11 Missense Variants.
authors: Andriessen, Evi; de Boer, Elke; Lyon, Gholson J; de Vries, Bert B A; Ockeloen, Charlotte W; Dingemans, Alexander J M
one_liner_zh: 该文利用AI表型框架PhenoScore预测ANKRD11错义变异致病性，但核心是临床表型与变异解读，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或结合建模，与课题无关。
abstract: KBG syndrome (KBGS, OMIM #148050) is a rare genetic disorder caused by heterozygous truncating or missense variants in the ANKRD11 gene or a deletion of 16q24.3 involving ANKRD11. While truncating variants clearly disrupt protein function, the interpretation of missense variants is more challenging, as many remain variants of uncertain significance (VUS). To address this, we evaluated PhenoScore, an open-source AI-based phenomics framework integrating facial recognition and medical data analysis, for predicting the pathogenicity of ANKRD11 missense variants and providing supporting evidence for variant interpretation within the ACMG framework, specifically the PP4 criterion. PhenoScore was trained on 79 individuals with truncating variants in ANKRD11 and age-, sex-, and ethnicity-matched controls with other neurodevelopmental disorders, and its performance was compared to AlphaMissense, REVEL, and the evaluation of a clinical geneticist. Six individuals with functionally confirmed pathogenic missense variants were used for testing. PhenoScore achieved high predictive accuracy with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.95 and a Brier score of 0.089, and pathogenic missense variants in the test set received a mean prediction score of 0.94. PhenoScore significantly outperformed REVEL (p < 0.01), especially in cases supported by functional and clinical evidence, while no significant difference was observed compared to AlphaMissense (p = 0.63); importantly, the two tools showed complementary strengths. These findings suggest that PhenoScore represents a promising tool for clinical variant interpretation, as it quantifies phenotypic concordance with KBGS and provides objective evidence that can strengthen the PP4 criterion within the ACMG framework. Combined with molecular prediction tools like AlphaMissense, PhenoScore may help reduce uncertainty surrounding VUS in ANKRD11 by complementing these scores.
abstract_zh: KBG综合征（KBGS，OMIM #148050）是一种罕见的遗传性疾病，由ANKRD11基因的杂合截短或错义变异，或涉及ANKRD11的16q24.3缺失引起。虽然截短变异明确破坏蛋白质功能，但错义变异的解读更具挑战性，因为许多仍属于意义不明确的变异（VUS）。为解决这一问题，我们评估了PhenoScore——一种基于人工智能的开源表型组学框架，整合面部识别和医学数据分析——用于预测ANKRD11错义变异的致病性，并在ACMG框架内为变异解读提供支持性证据，特别是PP4标准。PhenoScore在79名携带ANKRD11截短变异的个体及年龄、性别和种族匹配的患有其他神经发育障碍的对照组上进行了训练，其性能与AlphaMissense、REVEL及临床遗传学家的评估进行了比较。测试使用了六名经功能确认的致病性错义变异个体。PhenoScore实现了高预测准确性，曲线下面积（AUC）为0.95，Brier评分为0.089，测试集中的致病性错义变异平均预测得分为0.94。PhenoScore显著优于REVEL（p < 0.01），尤其是在有功能和临床证据支持的病例中，而与AlphaMissense相比未观察到显著差异（p = 0.63）；重要的是，这两种工具显示出互补优势。这些发现表明，PhenoScore是临床变异解读的有前景工具，因为它量化了与KBGS的表型一致性，并提供客观证据，可加强ACMG框架内的PP4标准。与AlphaMissense等分子预测工具结合使用时，PhenoScore可能通过补充这些评分，有助于减少ANKRD11中VUS的不确定性。
